Ask HN: Mass Loss in Black Hole Merger? How Does That Work?
items.snippet: Let's say we have two black holes, one 20 solar masses and the other 50 solar masses, and they get close enough and merge. In the process, they convert a solar mass or two into gravitational waves, which radiate off into the distance. Let me restate that, to emphasize what I think is really weird: A solar mass or two that is inside the event horizon got converted to energy and radiated outside the event horizon . E=mc^2. That part doesn't bother me. It's the "inside the event horizon" to "outside the event horizon" part that bothers me. Can someone ELI5 how that is possible? (Or even ELI20 with an undergrad in physics.)

items.title: Show HN: Free Image Merger – combine photos in-browser, nothing uploaded
Show HN: A local merge queue for parallel Claude Code agents
items.snippet: I have been pushing up to 90 commits a day on a MacBook Air via 4-5 parallel agents. As you can imagine when all the agents try to build, test and run dev servers on an 8GB machine it is the fast lane to a force quit and restart. I also did not want to pay the CI minutes on 90 pushes a day. So I designed a local merge queue to have all commits land one at a time and fully tested. Hopefully this helps other folks with more modest machines. Appreciate any feedback.

items.title: What if we learned languages like we acquired our first?
items.snippet: When we learn our mother tongue-language, we don't use dictionaries. We learn words in context, tied to an object, a situation, or a feeling. Memory relies heavily on these rich associations, but most language tools strip all of that away. This is something that frustrated me personally when i wanted to learn english and get better at it, so I built "Nattly" to help me learn English the same way native english speakers acquire it. Instead of isolated lists, Nattly ties vocabulary to specific scenarios and images, backed by spaced repetition. The goal is to practice recall based on context rather than just recognizing direct translations. Direct retrieval vs Recognition: The exposure gap is staggering. Children of native spaeker parents get thousands of hours of language exposure before they can speak, while adult learners may get just 15–30 hours a year. So I built a *Radio* feature in Nattly that generates everyday scenarios: The narrator plays the role of an image depiction of the scene taking place and occasionally explains difficult words directly in L2, helping learners build direct L2 associations rather than constantly translating through their native language L1.
